context.objective: Document how we carry out Financial Statement Creation, Review & Tie-Out, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.
The procedure says unresolved workbook differences are escalated to the Controller. How are those differences tracked and resolved afterward?

When a lead sheet does not tie to the trial balance, I as the Fund Accountant stop, investigate the usual causes like hidden rows, incomplete pastes, stale links or broken mappings, correct it, and rerun the check sheet. If I still cannot resolve it, it goes to the Controller. Nothing after that moves forward until it is fixed, so later work stays stopped or gets repeated. What we keep is the reconciliation and a resolution note with the workbook and check sheet. We require exact agreement, there is no materiality tolerance that lets a small difference pass. I do not know of a separate tracking log or tool for these, and who has final escalation authority beyond the Controller is not defined.
Once an unresolved difference reaches the Controller, what do they do to resolve it and let you know work can resume?

I do not know the exact steps the Controller takes on an escalated difference or how they formally signal that work can resume, that is not defined. What I can say is that the Controller does the detailed review of the workbook, the statement presentation and the tie-out, and returns unresolved differences or presentation issues to me for correction. I then correct, rerun the affected ties and the check sheet, and keep the resolution note. Work only continues once the lead sheets agree exactly to the trial balance. Whether there is any materiality policy that would let the Controller accept a difference is unconfirmed in practice, so today we treat exact agreement as required.
In the Controller’s detailed review, what do they check in the workbook, statement presentation, and tie-out?

I do not have a written checklist of what the Controller looks at, the approved checklist is still unresolved. From what I see, the Controller reviews that the lead sheets agree exactly to the trial balance, that footing recalculates and the cross-references on the marked tie-out PDF point to valid support, and the blacklines against the prior quarter and prior year-end, so that every unexpected wording, presentation or number change is explained or corrected. The Controller then returns comments, I resolve them and update all affected review records, and after that the Director does the final internal review before the approved draft goes to the client. One thing I should flag: where we compare to a comparable fund for presentation consistency, how that fund is selected and where the comparison record is kept is unconfirmed in practice. I only know it has to be a client-approved comparable fund. Deadlines for resolving review comments are also not set.
What typically starts your financial-statement preparation for a period?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

memo_findings.answer: The work is called Financial Statement Creation, Review & Tie-Out.
The documented work produces an internally reviewed, client-approved financial-statement package and supporting workpapers for distribution.

The procedure describes quarterly statement preparation and requires the period GL to be ready before TB extraction.
The event that initiates statement preparation and any fixed deadline remain unknown.
The procedure finishes with the client-approved clean package and workpapers uploaded, the marked PDF retained internally, upload evidence retained and the client notified.

The procedure assigns the Fund Accountant to confirm entity, quarter, audit status, required statements and Q4 footnotes; copy the approved prior package; compare it with prior quarter and year-end; and update current-period labels and contents.
The procedure directs the Fund Accountant to export the TB and account support from the GL, verify entity and period, and stop if GL completeness or report scope is not confirmed.
The procedure directs the Fund Accountant to populate TB, statement build, lead-sheet and check-sheet tabs; link statement lines to the TB or detailed schedules to lead sheets and lead-sheet totals to the TB; and validate cross-references and mappings.
The Fund Accountant says that if a lead sheet does not tie to the TB, they stop, investigate hidden rows, incomplete pastes, stale links or broken mappings, correct the issue and rerun the check sheet. Unresolved differences go to the Controller; later work remains stopped or is repeated until fixed.
After workbook reconciliation, the procedure has the Fund Accountant populate or link Word amounts, update investment positions, apply quarterly roll-forward rules and update references and formatting. Q4 footnotes are prepared when required using the LPA, schedules, prior footnotes and auditor/client input.
The procedure assigns the Fund Accountant to create a marked PDF tie-out, check footing and page references, tie statement lines to the TB and relevant schedules, recalculate investment percentages and flag matured notes or warrants for client consultation.
The procedure calls for blacklines against the prior quarter and year-end, and an approved comparable fund where applicable; unexpected changes are explained or corrected and the Controller reviews.
The documented review sequence is Fund Accountant preparer review, Controller detailed review and comments, Fund Accountant resolution and record updates, Director final internal review, then client review and comment resolution. Controller, Director and client approvals are retained.
After client approval, the procedure directs the Fund Accountant to retain the marked PDF in the digital binder, remove marks from the client copy, rename it, upload the clean PDF and required workpapers to Box, and notify the client.
The Fund Accountant says the Controller reviews the workbook, statement presentation and tie-out in detail and returns unresolved differences or presentation issues to them. The Fund Accountant corrects them, reruns affected ties and the check sheet, and keeps the resolution note; work continues only after exact lead-sheet-to-TB agreement.
The Fund Accountant reports that the Controller returns review comments, the Fund Accountant resolves them and updates affected review records, and the Director then performs final internal review before the approved draft goes to the client.

The Fund Accountant says current practice requires exact lead-sheet-to-TB agreement and unresolved differences block subsequent work. The reconciliation and resolution note are kept with the workbook and check sheet.
The Fund Accountant knows of no separate tracking log or tool, and final escalation authority beyond the Controller is undefined.
The procedure requires every displayed PDF amount and cross-reference to be supported and footing to recalculate; paste, formatting, ordering and source differences must be resolved before internal approval.
The method for selecting a comparable fund and the location of its comparison record remain unconfirmed. The procedure does not specify escalation of unresolved client comments.
The Fund Accountant does not know the Controller's exact steps on an escalated difference or how the Controller formally signals that work can resume.
From the Fund Accountant's observation, the Controller checks exact lead-sheet-to-TB agreement, recalculated footing and valid support for marked PDF cross-references, and reviews prior-quarter and prior-year-end blacklines for unexpected wording, presentation or numerical changes to be explained or corrected.
The Fund Accountant says deadlines for resolving review comments are not set.
The procedure adds footnote preparation and auditor/client input for Q4 or audited periods; Controller and Director review and auditor/client approval apply as appropriate.
The Fund Accountant reports that unresolved workbook differences stop later work or cause it to be repeated.

The supplied FA-12 procedure excerpt documents statement preparation, reconciliation, review and distribution.
Working artifacts include the prior approved statement package, TB and account support, linked workbook and check sheet, reconciliation and resolution note, marked PDF, blacklines, review notes and client correspondence.
Whether the supplied procedure as a whole reflects current practice remains to be confirmed.
The Fund Accountant has no written checklist of the Controller's review; the approved checklist remains unresolved.

The procedure describes fund financial statements, including entity and period confirmation, audited or unaudited presentation, partners' capital and potentially Q4 footnotes.
Whether the documented route is general GPFS practice remains unconfirmed.

The procedure uses the LPA and client/auditor requirements for presentation. It directs escalation of conflicts to the Controller and client; final resolution authority requires confirmation.
The procedure requires displayed Word amounts to trace to the reconciled workbook and prohibits manual overrides of controlled amounts without documented review and source support.
The Fund Accountant says current practice requires exact lead-sheet-to-TB agreement, including small differences.
Whether a materiality policy permits the Controller to accept a lead-sheet difference remains unconfirmed.
Where a comparable fund is used to assess presentation consistency, the Fund Accountant says it must be client-approved.
The documented statement work consumes the period GL's TB and detailed account support after the GL is ready, and requires client approval before final distribution.

The procedure identifies the GL as the source of TB and detail exports; Excel for linked statement and check sheets; Word and PDF for statement drafting and review; and a digital binder, Box and email for retention and distribution.
The procedure says the exact Box path, naming convention and distribution recipient list require client confirmation.
